summary: A 1914 wooden fire lookout on Schoodic Mountain, replaced in 1920 by a 24-foot steel tower; the cab is gone and sources disagree on what remained after a 2005 removal.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab no longer in place. A Forest Lookouts record notes a 2005 removal of the 'lookout structure' without saying what was removed.

access.note: The mountain lies within Donnell Pond public land and is reached by public trail from the Schoodic Beach parking area. The old tower itself is not documented as open to climbers.

visit.trail_note: Park at the Schoodic Beach parking area; the summit trail is about 1.3 miles one way, moderate.

events.note: Wooden lookout tower established on Schoodic Mountain; a six-mile telephone line from Franklin Station and a watchman's camp were built the same year.
Tower painted, new batteries installed and telephone lines repaired, per the 1916 Forest Commissioner's Report.
An October gale took the roof off the lookout; repairs included new roofing and shutters, and the lookout needed a new map and glass.
Watchmen Wendall Harrison and Howard Webb of North Sullivan are named for 1917-1919.
Maine Forestry District replaced the wooden tower with a 24-foot steel tower with cab.
Maine discontinued its staffed fire-tower network after a budget crisis; no source ties this date to the Schoodic tower specifically.
Forest Lookouts record reads 'Lookout structure removed' for 2005. FFLA still lists the tower standing with cab gone, so what was removed is unclear.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab gone. The Forest Lookouts record notes a 2005 'Lookout structure removed' without saying what that covered. The story reports both and does not choose.
Maine Memory says lookouts were manned from 1905 to 1973; Maine Atlas dates the end of the staffed network to 1991. The story uses the 1991 date from the state's own history page.

notes_for_editor: Build history is well documented (1914 wood, 1920 steel with cab), and the brief's height (7.3 m, 24 ft) matches. Status is the open question: FFLA lists it as standing with cab gone, but the Forest Lookouts record gives a 2005 'Lookout structure removed' with no detail; no modern photo or visit report was found. Staffing is inferred from the statewide 1991 end of the network, not a tower-specific record. Access rests on the public Donnell Pond trail; whether the old tower itself is climbable is unverified, so no climbable flag is set. Watchmen 1917-1919 come from a photo caption only. The brief's agency name is kept as the historical Maine Forestry District. Maine Memory record 1514 (ca. 1920) is a photo candidate, not added because its licence was not checked. Recommend a site visit or a current photo before any status claim is strengthened.
